I'm treating this termination as a contractor-to-employee conversion, not a departure. Hana Nguyen's contingent record (C5001, `1391f9b9dbc799b0121b28004e6f5a94`) ends on 2026-11-02, and an active employee record for her starts the same day (E1023, `37b4000bd1c51f86973082d609b4e5d2`). The new record has the same tokenised government ID and says it was converted from C5001. Org policy for conversions is `carry_over`, so she keeps her current identity account, pointed at the new record. No escalation is needed.

**What I found (as of 2026-11-02, 00:04)**
- **Identity:** her account `acct-4f73fd94` (hana.nguyen@example.com) is enabled with one active session. Its groups (All-Staff, Eng-Git, VPN-Users) are exactly the standard access for Software Engineer, and none are privileged. Her job, org, manager and cost center are the same on both records, so no group changes are needed.
- **New record (E1023):** no identity account, no work email in Workday, no finance profile. Both onboarding tasks are "Not Started".
- **Old record (C5001):** no legal hold, no corporate card, no open expense reports, and nobody's expenses are routed to her for approval. Her laptop (`tkt-eq-C5001`, Fulfilled) stays with her.

**What the plan deliberately leaves out:** no disabling, session revocation, licence removal, mailbox conversion or deletion, asset recovery, card deactivation or closing of expense reports. Doing any of these would cut off a current employee, and there is nothing to close anyway. I also left out final pay: contingent workers aren't normally paid through payroll, and irreversible steps should only run when clearly required. The new HIRE event for E1023 isn't in the feed yet, so if it arrives it belongs to this same case and needs no separate handling.

**One judgement call:** the "Provision equipment" task counts as complete once an equipment order exists. I plan to close it using her existing fulfilled order instead of buying a duplicate laptop.

I moved Hana Nguyen's account, acct-4f73fd94 (hana.nguyen@example.com), to her new employee worker record. Re-reading the account confirmed it worked.

**Why this is a conversion, not a real termination:**
- **Same person:** the old contractor record (1391f9b9dbc799b0121b28004e6f5a94, C5001) ends on 2026-11-02. The new employee record (37b4000bd1c51f86973082d609b4e5d2, E1023) starts that same day.
- **Records link up:** both records have the same tokenised government ID (gid-427a3595d06a), and the new one says it was converted from C5001.
- **Policy:** for contractor-to-employee conversions, the org policy is to keep the existing account.
- **No duplicate:** no other account was already linked to the new worker record.

**What I did:** I relinked acct-4f73fd94 to worker 37b4000bd1c51f86973082d609b4e5d2 with employee type Employee. The relink tool has no idempotency key field, so I couldn't use case-d9bc1d97-relink. I called it only once.

**Confirmed on re-read:**
- Linked to the new worker record, with employee type Employee.
- Still enabled, with its 1 active session.
- Still has the Office-E3 licence and the user mailbox.
- Still in All-Staff, Eng-Git and VPN-Users.

I didn't disable the account, revoke sessions, remove licences or change the mailbox.

**Left for others (not identity work):** the new Workday record E1023 has no work email yet. Someone needs to write hana.nguyen@example.com back to Workday.

- I wrote hana.nguyen@example.com to worker 37b4000bd1c51f86973082d609b4e5d2 (E1023), using correlation_id case-d9bc1d97 and idempotency key case-d9bc1d97-email.
- The Workday process (event 82458cc89f7a7dafb43adc4fc7af3626) showed "Successfully Completed" on the second check.
- Re-reading the record confirmed the work email is now hana.nguyen@example.com.

**Step 3 – Onboarding task**
- I set task 75fa6dd891fde85ce69bae29f652d008 ("Create accounts and email") to Complete. Workday's options are "In Progress" and "Complete", so that is the status the plan's "Completed" refers to.
- Re-reading her tasks confirmed it shows Complete.

**Not mine to do:** her "Provision equipment" task (deb0e066de26e655d3f21dcc2be88b46) is still Not Started. It's marked complete once an equipment order is placed, which isn't Workday work, so I left it.

I created the finance profile for Hana Nguyen's new employee record (worker 37b4000bd1c51f86973082d609b4e5d2, E1023), and re-reading it confirms it's in place. This was step 4 of case-d9bc1d97.

- **Cost center:** Workday cost center 1e2feb89414c343c1027c4d1c386bbc4 translates to Finance code CC-1000.
- **Workday record matches the plan:** the record is Active, type Employee, hire date 2026-11-02, cost center CC-1000 Engineering. Her manager is Avery Carter (afbd67f9619699cfe1988ad9f06c144a), and the record says she was converted from contractor record C5001.

**Not done, as the plan said:** I didn't request final pay, deactivate a card or close expense reports for her old contractor record (1391f9b9dbc799b0121b28004e6f5a94, C5001). I didn't re-check that record's finance profile myself; the plan says it has no active card and no open reports. Ending a contractor assignment because she's becoming an employee doesn't clearly call for final pay.

Nothing in finance is left open. Her "Provision equipment" task, which the Workday team flagged, isn't finance work, so I left it.

**Do not run the normal new-hire steps for case-f9495568.** Creating an account, finance profile or equipment order would make a second account, a second finance profile or an unneeded laptop order.
